articles.title: Geelong fined $140,000 over secret Jake Kolodjashnij concussion waiver
articles.summary: AFL sanctions Cats for failing to lodge variation to player’s contract. Findings clear a path for waivers to be implemented in future. The AFL has punished Geelong for their high-profile “mistakes” in managing head injury risks with a vulnerable player, but has not found anything wrong with clubs…
body: The league fined the Cats $100,000 on Thursday for failing to inform it of a change to Jake Kolodjashnij’s contract, previously described as a “waiver” by AFL Commission chair and former Cats president Craig Drummond.

The sanction also activated a $40,000 suspended fine applied to Geelong for salary cap-related breaches last year, leaving the club with a $140,000 penalty to be paid into the AFL’s injury and support fund. The Cats recorded a profit of $1.7m last year.

The clause was drafted and signed after the defender was not fully cleared by the AFL’s concussion panel in 2024, and followed consultation about potential risks of returning to senior football with the player, his family, doctors and insurers. The waiver was set aside by Geelong in the days after its existence first became public.
The AFL Commission found the Cats did not intend to conceal the agreement, however, in accepting the recommendations from an investigation by Kings Counsel James Peters.

articles.title: Muchová and Menšík win $1m US Open mixed doubles title in late-night thriller
articles.summary: Czech pair beat Bencic and Cobolli in deciding tiebreak. Revamped event draws strong crowds at Arthur Ashe. Singles stars dominate after doubles specialists exit. To many who came to the US Open grounds this week, the showpiece of the mixed doubles championship came Tuesday afternoon, with the…
body: To the players who remained in the field after Williams and Alcaraz exited in the quarter-finals, the real highlight was Wednesday night’s final at Arthur Ashe Stadium, with its $1m in prize money on the line. Karolína Muchová and Jakub Menšík made the most of the spotlight, beating Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli 6-3, 1-6 (10-6) for the title.

Their win capped an event that, in a reversal of recent years, was dominated by singles players instead of doubles specialists. The Czech duo beat Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev 5-4 (8-6) 3-5 (11-9) and the runners-up bested Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils 4-5 (7-9) 4-1 (10-5) in a pair of competitive semi-finals that each lasted over an hour, making for a final that finished just before midnight.

“This format of a tournament, it went really quickly,” said Muchová, who was playing her first matches since losing the Wimbledon final in June. “I’m obviously super happy that we managed to win. It was not my expectation.”

articles.title: Watson to face fellow Briton Dart for US Open spot
articles.summary: Heather Watson will face compatriot Harriet Dart for a place in the US Open main draw as six British players reach the final qualifying round.
body: Heather Watson and Harriet Dart will go head-to-head for a place in the US Open main draw as six British players made it through to the third and final qualifying round in New York.
Watson kept alive her hopes of a first US Open singles main-draw appearance in five years by overcoming Spain's Angela Fita Boluda in a rollercoaster encounter lasting nearly three hours.
The 34-year-old was twice a break up in the third set and served for the match - only to be taken to a deciding 10-point tie-break.
However, she held her nerve to seal a 6-4 5-7 7-6 (10-5) win.

articles.title: Roger Goodell says NFL is reviewing Jed York’s arrest under personal conduct policy
articles.summary: Goodell confirms review after Ohio prostitution sting. York pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges. NFL has previously disciplined owners for misconduct. Commissioner Roger Goodell said the NFL is looking into whether San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York will be punished for violating the…
body: “It’s being reviewed under the personal conduct policy,” Goodell said Wednesday at the owners’ meetings in Atlanta. “We’ll do that and when there’s something to be reported we’ll talk.”
York was arrested in a mobile home park by the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force after police said he was attempting to pay $160 for sex with a woman he believed to be a prostitute.

He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offenses to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest. He also was fined $1,150. Police seized the $160 from York and that was later given to the human trafficking task force as part of the plea. York also completed an online course.
York has spent most of the summer in Ohio, where he grew up near Youngstown. He had filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, in May, according to court records.

articles.title: NFL finally calls time on beleaguered Pro Bowl after years of format changes
articles.summary: League ends flag football and skills competitions. Only original 88 selections will earn Pro Bowl status. Players to be honored at Super Bowl week in LA. The NFL is ending the Pro Bowl Games after repeated format changes to its annual all-star event.
body: Beginning ⁠with the 2026 season, 88 Pro Bowlers will be selected but the NFL no longer plans to stage an ⁠AFC-NFC game, a ⁠flag-football matchup ​or an accompanying series of competitions. The players chosen will instead be invited to next year’s Super Bowl site in ⁠Los Angeles for an in-person celebration in February.

The biggest change beyond eliminating the event itself involves alternates. Only the original 88 ⁠selections will be named Pro Bowlers and no alternates will be added, ending ​a system that expanded the list ‌when players withdrew because of ‌injuries, Super Bowl commitments or other reasons.
Voting remains split with fans, players ‌and coaches accounting for one-third of the selection process.

The NFL ​reworked the event through multiple iterations in recent years as interest in the traditional tackle all-star game declined. The AFC-NFC format was temporarily replaced by a fantasy football style draft in 2014 before later returning in 2017. The Pro Bowl ⁠moved away from longtime host Hawaii after the 2016 edition.

articles.title: Columbus Crew fall to Club América 2-0 in Leagues Cup quarterfinal
articles.summary: Switching to the Leagues Cup quarterfinals didn't help the Crew end a losing streak that grew to four straight defeats across all competitions after a 2-0 loss to Club América of Liga MX on Aug. 27 at Dignity Health Sports Park in Carson, California.
body: Despite applying offensive pressure for most of the game, they couldn't get a single shot past Club América goalkeeper Rodolpho Cota in a frustrating night at the home stadium of the L.A. Galaxy. Club America built a 2-0 lead at the half on goals by Raphael Veiga in the 11th minute and Brian Rodriguez in the sixth minute of stoppage time.

Rodriguez assisted on the goal by Veiga, who returned the favor for Rodriguez shortly before the whistle ended the half. About six minutes prior to Rodriguez's goal, Crew forward Brais Mendez was stopped cold by Cota on a penalty kick from the center of the box that could've tied it 1-1 in the 40th minute.

It was one of several highlights for Cota, who finished with eight saves for a shutout in a game the Crew put eight of 18 shots on target and generated a sizeable edge of 3.2 to 1.9 in expected goals.

Cota made two big stops against great looks for Crew forward Josef Martinez, who made his first start for Columbus, and the Club America goalkeeper also got help from the left goal post in the 18th minute to stop Cesar Ruvalcaba off a corner kick.

articles.summary: Barcelona will play their first home LaLiga fixture of the season at the Camp Nou on Thursday, hosting Athletic Club in a midweek encounter. The hosts arrive in excellent form after an emphatic 5-0 victory over Elche that launched their campaign.
body: FC Barcelona look set to hand a long-awaited club debut to high-profile summer signing Rodri, who has completed successive training sessions following a minor back operation and is expected to be named among the substitutes.
Flick appears ready to tweak his back line at the Spotify Camp Nou, with Pau Cubarsí, Jules Koundé and João Cancelo likely to return to the starting XI after being rested last time out.

The Catalans do, however, face a midfield concern as Gavi is doubtful after suffering a heavy knee contusion against Elche; scans excluded a serious ligament injury, but he missed the squad’s final training session.

Gavi joins established absentees Frenkie de Jong, who is recovering from a knee problem, and Roony Bardghji. Joan García is forecast to start in goal, shielded by Andreas Christensen alongside Cubarsí.

articles.title: Super Bowl champions Seahawks to be sold in record $9.6bn deal
articles.summary: NFL owners approve the $9.612bn record sale of the reigning Super Bowl champions Seattle Seahawks to a group led by billionaire Vinod Khosla.
body: The deal, which required the support of at least 24 of 32 owners, is currently the second highest amount paid for a franchise in North American sports history.
The estate of Paul G. Allen, which inherited the NFL team after the death of the Microsoft co-founder in 2018, agreed to terms with the Khosla family on 11 July after a search for a new owner.

And now approved, the sale surpasses the $6.05bn the Washington Commanders fetched when they were sold in 2023, although the NBA's Los Angeles Lakers were subsequently sold for $10bn in 2025 and are currently in the process of changing ownership again for a reported $12.5bn.
"We are honoured to be entrusted as the next stewards of the Seattle Seahawks. How often do you get to buy a franchise that just won the Super Bowl?" said Khosla.

articles.title: Chelsea vs Luton Town – Match preview and team news
articles.summary: Chelsea’s Carabao Cup campaign begins at Stamford Bridge on Thursday against a Luton Town side still chasing a repeat of their sole major trophy, the 1988 League Cup. History is firmly against the visitors: Luton have been eliminated in eight of their last nine EFL Cup ties against Premier League…
body: Chelsea 's Carabao Cup campaign begins at Stamford Bridge on Thursday against a Luton Town side still chasing a repeat of their sole major trophy, the 1988 League Cup.

Luton head into the match unbeaten across three fixtures this season, coming from behind to beat Reading 4-3 on the opening weekend before a 2-2 draw with newly-promoted Notts County and a 3-0 win over Gillingham in the first round. Chelsea, by contrast, are still finding their feet under Xabi Alonso, whose competitive debut brought a 3-2 win at Fulham three days earlier. Thursday offers the new head coach an early look at squad depth before a testing run of fixtures ahead.

Jordan Henderson (wrist) and Emmanuel Emegha (hamstring) remain sidelined, and Wesley Fofana is suspended, serving the second of a two-match ban carried over from a red card against Sunderland last season. Moises Caicedo and Marco Palestra both missed the win at Fulham after picking up injuries in training and remain doubts, with Caicedo more likely to return for the weekend. Alonso is expected to make wholesale changes and could hand full debuts to several summer signings.

articles.title: Fulham vs AFC Wimbledon – Match preview and team news
articles.summary: Craven Cottage stages a first-ever competitive meeting between Fulham and AFC Wimbledon on Thursday, with a place in the Carabao Cup third round at stake. Fulham enter off the back of a narrow 2-3 defeat to Chelsea on the Premier League’s opening weekend, Alvaro Arbeloa’s first game in charge…
body: Wimbledon reached this stage only after Callum Maycock 's dramatic 97th-minute equaliser forced a penalty shootout against Newport County, which the Dons went on to win. Fulham, whose 146-year history has never produced a major trophy, reached the Carabao Cup quarter-finals last season and will see this competition as a realistic route to silverware. Steven Sessegnon, who began his career at Fulham before moving on, could line up for Wimbledon against his former club.

Captain Tom Cairney remains sidelined with a knee injury and is not expected back until later in the autumn. Joachim Andersen is available again having served the final match of a three-game suspension against Chelsea, though Arbeloa may still use the tie to rest him. Several substitutes from the Chelsea game, including Ryan Sessegnon, Rodrigo Muniz, Harrison Reed and Shea Charles, are pushing for starts.

Johnnie Jackson has no confirmed unavailable players, giving him a fully fit squad to select from. Veteran defender Andy Yiadom is available and could make his full debut for the club. Callum Maycock, whose stoppage-time equaliser rescued the first-round tie against Newport County, is among those pushing for inclusion.

The sight of Gonzalez walking out at the sold-out stadium before the 3-2 win against West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup second round was a welcome one for head coach Matthias Jaissle, who desperately wanted him.
The German stressed he was "always a believer in the positive things", but tellingly also referred to the pursuit as a "long fight".

articles.title: Czech duo collect $1m after winning US Open mixed doubles championship
articles.summary: Czech duo Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik defeated Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli 6-3 1-6 [10-6] to win the US Open mixed doubles championship and scoop the $1m grand prize on Wednesday night.
body: Muchova and Mensik rallied from 3-0 and 8-5 down and then saved two match points to defeat Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev in a thrilling contest 5-4 (8-6) 3-5 [11-9] to reach the final.
The all-Czech team, sported matching pink-top, maroon-bottom outfits, then delivered in the second-match tie-break against Indian Wells champions Bencic and Cobolli to win the title.

"The matching outfit made the difference for us," joked Muchova, who suffered a heart-breaking three-set defeat to Linda Noskova in the Wimbledon final last month. "No really, I wasn't expecting to be standing here. Thanks Jakub for carrying me through this event.
"I wasn't really expecting to ​be standing here tonight. We came out just to ​have fun and enjoy these mixed doubles and now we are ​standing here. So we did something right."

articles.title: Thomas Castellanos joins Texas Tech as Big 12 confirms QB is eligible
articles.summary: The former Florida State quarterback remains eligible under the Big 12's new pro-athlete rules after attending an NFL minicamp without signing a contract, positioning him to back up Will Hammond in Lubbock.
body: Former Florida State quarterback Thomas Castellanos has signed with Texas Tech out of the transfer portal, just days after a Kentucky judge granted a temporary injunction in an eligibility lawsuit that included Castellanos and former Missouri basketball standout Mark Mitchell.
Because Castellanos has an injunction, he will not be affected by the new ruling in the Colorado lawsuit that took away eligibility for qualified athletes in the Class of 2022.

More importantly as it relates to his decision to play for Texas Tech, Castellanos would still be eligible even after the Big 12 Conference unanimously adopted a rule barring institutions from fielding professional athletes. The 5-foot-9 Castellanos competed as a wide receiver during the Miami Dolphins' rookie minicamp in May but because he went undrafted and did not sign a contract with Miami, he will be eligible to play this fall, a league spokesperson told CBS Sports' Richard Johnson.

The Big 12 made its announcement Wednesday -- hours after Castellanos committed to Texas Tech -- in the wake of the SEC and Big Ten enacting bans on the glut of pro athletes looking to return to college athletics.
